summary.headline: Anand Rathi Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR2,732 million and PAT rose 50% to INR419 million, a record quarter per management.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 20% YoY to INR2,732 million, with PAT up 50% YoY to INR419 million at a 15% margin. H1 revenue rose 21% to INR5,193 million; H1 PAT after exceptional items was INR653 million (up 29%), and PAT before exceptional items was INR810 million (up 60%). Broking and related services grew 34% YoY to INR1,551 million, while the MTF book reached INR14,993 million at 30 September, already about 57% of the year-end guidance. Management said market volumes were weak in derivatives but cash volumes were improving, and it discussed the drop in net cash, which it attributed to clients moving margins from FDs into G-Secs.

financial_highlights.change: Q2 distribution income up about 4% YoY per analyst question; not confirmed by management

segments.name: Broking and related services
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR1,551 million (+34% YoY); H1 INR2,831 million (+25% YoY). Equity cash is 52% of broking revenue. Digital platform contributed 36% of brokerage income in H1.

segments.name: Margin trading facility (MTF)
segments.commentary: Book INR14,993 million at 30 Sep 2026 against year-end guidance of INR17,500-18,000 million. Q2 MTF book grew 38% YoY to INR1,499 crore; MTF interest income INR496 million in Q2 (+36%) and INR924 million in H1 (+43%). Borrowing cost about 9.5%, NIM about 4.5%, zero NPAs, average book per client below INR17 lakh.

segments.name: Distribution and non-broking
segments.commentary: Distribution AUM INR99,990 million, up 29% YoY. Distribution income INR327 million in Q2 and INR603 million in H1. Trail income now covers about 75% of salary costs, per management.

segments.name: Asset management and custody
segments.commentary: Asset management grew 29% YoY to INR99,990 million. Under custody grew about 13% YoY to about INR1.15 trillion.

guidance_outlook: Year-end MTF book target of INR1,750-1,800 crore, which the MTF figures in the call suggest is a different scale from the INR17,500-18,000 million year-end guidance quoted by the WTD; the two figures are inconsistent and need checking.
Distribution AUM to grow about 40% by end of FY27; management said it had already reached 29% growth by September.
Broking revenue targeted to grow 15-20% and non-broking 30-35% (up to 40% in some cases).
Long-term target: top line growth of about 15-20% and bottom line growth of about 20-25% to 30%.
capex_capacity: Network at 30 Sep 2026: 99 branches and 1,071 authorised persons across 314 cities.
Client base about 10.5 lakh, of which 55% have been with the firm for more than 3 years and 71% of active clients are in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.
Employee base grew: management said it adds about 150 employees on an ongoing basis; Q2 employee expenses rose about 31% YoY, partly from bringing outsourced staff onto payroll.
New products: insurance is being stabilised, AIF is being added to distribution, and an NRI business is being built.
demand_pricing: Nifty 50 fell 5.22% in the quarter and 1.3% in H1, including a 6% fall in September. IPO activity was strong: 108 IPOs raised about INR90,000 crore in Q2, and H1 raised INR96,585 crore across 154 mainboard IPOs.
Industry MTF book was INR156,261 crore as of 12 Oct 2026, up about 41% YoY. Demat accounts were about 24 crore, with 31.1 lakh added in September.

Management said cash-market volumes were improving while F&O and capital-market volumes were flat to lower. It said Anand Rathi's broking growth outperformed the industry because it has no proprietary trading volumes.
Distribution income growth lagged AUM growth because of upfront commissions in the prior year and the RBI/AMFI ARN transfer cooling period, which was extended from 6 to 12 months.
Around INR300 crore of MTF-related impact from an RBI circular was absorbed, and borrowing costs were held at around 9.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did distribution income grow only 4% when distribution AUM grew 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed upfront commissions earned in the prior year that did not repeat, plus a longer 12-month ARN transfer cooling period. It said trail income is rising and now covers about 75% of salaries.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee expenses rise about 31% in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outsourced staff were moved onto the payroll, which it called largely one-time. It also said it keeps adding RMs and product staff, about 150 employees on an ongoing basis.

qa_highlights.question: Have trading volumes recovered since Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cash-market volumes were growing consistently while derivatives and capital-market volumes were static or lower. Broking revenue is tracking cash volumes.

qa_highlights.question: How is MTF spread and risk managed?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing cost is about 9.5% and NIM about 4.5%. Average book per client is below INR17 lakh, and the company says its MTF NPA has been zero for 8 years. Policy has not changed; the stock list is about 1,000 approved stocks out of about 2,000 permitted.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net cash fall from about INR2,700 crore to about INR900 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said HNI clients moved margin cash from FDs into G-Secs following an RBI circular. Business is intact, and the decline reflects a change in the form of client margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt-market strategy with yields above 7.40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt is a small allocation for clients. It sees rising rates in the next 3-6 months and recommends short-term G-Sec allocation only, with equity preferred over the long term.

risks_watch: Derivatives and capital-market volumes remain weak, and broking growth depends on cash-market volumes.
Net cash fell sharply (about INR2,700 crore to about INR900 crore) on the client margin shift to G-Secs. Watch whether this affects liquidity and interest income.
Distribution income lagged AUM growth. Track whether trail income catches up as management expects.
Employee costs rose about 31% YoY in Q2, and the company plans ongoing hiring. Watch the operating margin.
Rising interest rates may affect the MTF spread and the borrowing cost, which is about 9.5%.
Inconsistent MTF targets in the transcript (INR1,750-1,800 crore vs INR17,500-18,000 million) need clarification.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and on MTF asset quality, saying the book is at zero NPAs and that guidance is already largely met. It was more defensive on the distribution income gap and the net cash decline, which it attributed to a change in client margin format.
key_quotes: I'm happy to share with all of you that the last quarter, we have achieved our highest ever revenue as well as higher ever profitability.
Considering all those facts, our NPA into MTF book is zero.
Business-wise, business is intact, and cash flow -wise, it's just a change format change in cash flow.

growth.why: Management guides medium-term top-line growth of 15-20% (broking 15-20%, non-broking 30-35%) and FY27 MTF book of INR1,750-1,800 crore, with H1 MTF already ~57% of target and distribution AUM at +29% against a ~40% FY27 goal; backing is partly specific (MTF book, AUM) but no capacity additions are cited.
